name: Antonovka seedling

origin.place: seed of the old Russian cultivar Antonovka
origin.note: Long used for hardy standard trees and framestocks in Russia, Poland, Canada and the northern US.

soil_notes: wide soil tolerance; deep root system copes with grass competition and lean ground
best_for: full-size standards and hardy framestocks in very cold climates; orchards and homesteads planted for longevity
avoid_when: small gardens or anyone wanting early crops
variety_fit: A hardy root and frame for tender varieties in cold regions; spur-type or weak varieties keep trees more manageable.
notes: Seedlings of the very hardy Russian cultivar Antonovka give full-size, deep-rooted, free-standing trees and are a traditional choice for cold-climate standards and hardy framestocks. As seedlings they vary in vigour and behaviour from tree to tree, and trees are slow to come into bearing. Their main value is root hardiness where clonal dwarfing stocks would be killed by frost.

name: Robusta 5

origin.place: Ottawa Research Station (Central Experimental Farm), Ontario
origin.parentage: Malus x robusta, thought to be M. baccata x M. prunifolia
origin.note: Year is its introduction as a rootstock; parent of most Geneva rootstocks (source of fire blight, woolly aphid and replant resistance).

soil_notes: vigorous root system; suits lean soils and replant ground
best_for: very hardy standard trees in cold regions, especially under spur-type varieties
avoid_when: small gardens or high-density plantings - far too vigorous
variety_fit: Best used only under spur-type varieties because of its vigour.
notes: A very vigorous, very winter-hardy Canadian crab-hybrid stock that produces standard-size trees and breaks bud very early in spring. It resists fire blight and powdery mildew, is immune to woolly apple aphid and tolerates replant disease, which is why it is a parent of most Geneva rootstocks. Too vigorous for modern orchards except under spur-type varieties.

name: Apple seedling (open-pollinated)
clones: McIntosh, Delicious or Golden Delicious seed (North America)

origin.note: The seed source sets vigour, hardiness and uniformity; the oldest kind of apple rootstock.

soil_notes: widely adapted; tolerates poor, stony or grassed ground and needs little irrigation once established
best_for: traditional standards, meadow and community orchards, wildlife and grazing orchards, long-lived trees
avoid_when: small gardens, trained forms, or when early and uniform cropping matters
variety_fit: Useful under spur-type or weak varieties; triploids and vigorous varieties make very large trees.
notes: The traditional standard: seedling roots give large, long-lived, well-anchored trees that tolerate poor or grassed ground, but they are slow to crop and less uniform than clonal stocks because every seedling differs. Seedlings start free of the latent viruses carried by clonal material. The seed source matters - e.g. Antonovka for hardiness, Bittenfelder for German meadow orchards.

name: Crab C

origin.note: One of the clonal stocks East Malling selected from 'free' and 'crab' seedling populations; used mainly in research.

notes: A vigorous clonal crab stock from East Malling's work on selecting rootstocks from crab seedlings; later trials used it as a vigorous interstem, which gave more growth than trees on M.2 alone. It never became a commercial rootstock and few horticultural data have been published. It is not the same thing as hardy Malus baccata (Siberian crab) seedling stocks, which have their own record.

name: Siberian crab (Malus baccata) seedling

origin.place: species native to Siberia, northern China and Mongolia
origin.note: Long the usual root for apples on the Canadian prairies and in Alaska.

soil_notes: few soil-specific data; valued for root survival in extreme cold rather than soil tolerance
best_for: the coldest apple-growing areas (prairies, Alaska, zones 2-3) where other roots freeze
avoid_when: mild climates where hardiness is not needed and a clonal stock gives better size control
variety_fit: Widely used with prairie-hardy varieties; tender varieties are often grown on it with a hardy interstem. Budding low is preferred to whip-and-tongue grafting where unions have blown out.
notes: The hardiest apple understock: Siberian crab seedlings have survived about -45 C with little snow cover and give tough, well-anchored trees, and most older apple trees in places like Edmonton stand on them. Vigour and behaviour vary from seedling to seedling and few size or yield data are published. The Finnish selection YP, from open-pollinated M. baccata, is reported vigorous, productive and hardy but fire blight susceptible.
